text:
sara: quick heads-up — ran a canary of the new kernel-selector heuristic + microbatch tuning against canary traffic (config: microbatch_interval=2ms, coalesce_delay=0.8ms, jitter=off). noticed an unexpected p95/p99 tail regression on requests with large KV footprints. logs + perf below.
ian: ouch. how big is "large KV" for this run?
sara: KV entries ~2.2M keys active, median seq_len 512, some requests hitting KV priming path. KV hit_rate dropped to ~0.72 under the canary (was ~0.89 on baseline kernel).
margo: do you have the kernel selection diff? maybe the new heuristic prefers the single-pass kernel that trades off KV locality?
sara: yeah — selector now chooses kernel_v2 for medium-seq models when batch_size_estimate > 8. v2 improves raw throughput on short sequences but seems to thrash KV LRU when microbatches are very tight. pasted quick profiling snippet:```
# perf-summary
kernel_select: kernel_v2 chosen for 67% of batches
hotpath: kernel_v2_dispatch (48% CPU)
kv_manager: eviction_writes up 3.1x
batch_formation: mean_hold_ms=1.9 (config 2ms)
queueing: Q.len_p50=2 Q.len_p99=12
latency_p95: baseline 98ms -> canary 176ms
latency_p99: baseline 180ms -> canary 310ms
throughput_tokens_s: baseline 13.2k -> canary 12.1k
```
liam: interesting — so lower throughput + worse tail. Could be increased KV evictions causing extra prefetch/KV writeback on kernel switch. any kernel-specific prefetch changes?
sara: kernel_v2 does an opportunistic KV priming pass that assumes stable coalescing; with jitter off we see microbatches align and cause repeated priming for overlapping windows. that + smaller microbatch interval means more frequent priming.
ian: try enabling jitter and increase microbatch_interval to 4ms as a quick A/B? add a tiny random [0..1.5ms] jitter to break alignment.
sara: ran that in a follow-up canary (microbatch_interval=4ms jitter=U(0,1.5ms)). results: p95 dropped back near baseline, p99 improved but still slightly worse than baseline. new numbers: p95=105ms p99=195ms token_throughput=12.9k kv_hit=0.85
margo: suggests alignment was a major factor. Could also tune selector to prefer kernel_v1 when kv_hit_rate < 0.8 or when active_kv_entries > 1.5M.
liam: what about queue policy? are we FIFO or are we hedging small-latency requests?
sara: we were using FIFO with token_budget_target=2048. I tried lowering token_budget_target to 1536 for the canary which bumped batch_size_estimate down and reduced kernel_v2 selection frequency. that also helped tails.
perf-bot: infra perf alert — regression detected: p99 increased by 72% on canary cluster. linked perf scan: https://perf.redwood/internal/scans/1785439000
ian: plan: 1) revert the aggressive kernel_v2 selector conditionally (kv-heavy fallback) 2) enable small jitter default for microbatch_interval <= 3ms 3) add selector metric kv_hit_estimate into decision (threshold 0.82) 4) run a controlled A/B with token_budget_target=1536 vs 2048.
sara: I've pushed a TL;DR patch:```diff
- if batch_size_est > 8: choose kernel_v2
+ if batch_size_est > 8 and kv_hit_estimate > 0.82: choose kernel_v2
+ else: stick with kernel_v1 to preserve KV locality
```
margo: also add a quick circuit: if observed eviction_writes/sec > baseline*1.5 then prefer kernel_v1 for the next 30s.
liam: add an experiment in the rollout plan to vary jitter amplitude and microbatch interval separately and record kv_hit, eviction_writes, p99. small grid: interval {2,4,6}ms x jitter_amp {0,1.5,3}ms.
sara: noted. I'll schedule the grid, include kernel selector flag, and put perf results in the canary dashboard. will also attach the flamegraphs.
ian: awesome. thanks — this matches my hypothesis about alignment-driven KV churn. once we have matrix results we can tune defaults and update the selector. :thumbsup:
liam: thanks — cc'ing platform on potential default change.
perf-bot: next_canary_job_id=1785439125 started for grid run.
